worked.problem: A sample space has 7 outcomes: A-only 3, B-only 3, both 0, neither 1. Find P(A or B).
actions: Mark the four disjoint regions A-only=3, overlap=0, B-only=3, outside=1.
Calculate |A|=3 and |B|=3; use the common denominator |S|=7.
|A∪B|=3+3−0=6; the overlap was counted twice in |A|+|B|.
The requested favourable count for A or B is 6; divide by 7.
Answer: P(A or B) = 6/7. All four disjoint regions add to 7.
worked.check: Answer: P(A or B) = 6/7. All four disjoint regions add to 7.
worked.misconception: The overlap is counted once in a union; complement requires both disjointness and exhaustive coverage.
